title: Field based pilot-scale drinking water distribution system: Simulation of long hydraulic retention times and microbiological mediated monochloramine decay
author: Kulkarni, Awad, et al.

steps.title: Collect and analyse water chemistry
steps.instruction: Collect water samples three times per month from the pilot‑scale distribution system (PDS) at the inflow, 300 m, 600 m and 900 m (outflow) points. Immediately after collection measure free and total chlorine (mg L⁻¹) with a DR 2800™ spectrophotometer (HACH, Australia) at the TBWTP; calculate monochloramine as total minus free chlorine. Verify monochloramine by the DPD‑Ferrous titrimetric method (Standard Method 4500‑Cl F). Measure pH on‑site with a WP‑91 portable pH meter (TPS Instruments) and record temperature with a TR‑10 digital thermometer (Elitech). Determine nitrate and nitrite concentrations using a Spectroquant NOVA 60 (MERCK, Australia) with cell test numbers 109713 (nitrate) and 114547 (nitrite).

steps.title: Neutralise and filter water for DNA
steps.instruction: At the PDS outflow (May 2017) collect 500 mL of water in RNase/DNase‑free bottles and immediately dose with sodium thiosulfate to a final concentration of 18 mg L⁻¹ to quench residual chlorine. Transport samples to the laboratory and, as soon as possible, vacuum‑filter each sample through a 47 mm sterile plain cellulose nitrate membrane (0.1 µm pore size, Whatman, GE Healthcare Life Science).

steps.title: Extract DNA from filtered water
steps.instruction: Extract DNA from each filter using the DNeasy PowerWater kit (Qiagen, NSW, Australia) following the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Collect and process biofilm material
steps.instruction: In February 2018 cut ~4 cm sections of PE pipe from the biofilm collectors, place each piece into a sterile 50 mL Nunc conical centrifuge tube and keep on ice during transport. In the laboratory detach biofilm by vigorously scraping the inner surface with RNase/DNase‑free sterile antistatic spatulas until the surface is clean. Weigh approximately 0.20 g of recovered biofilm and transfer into a 2 mL collection tube.

steps.title: Lyse biofilm and isolate DNA
steps.instruction: Suspend the 0.20 g biofilm in 350 µL cell‑lysis solution from the DNeasy PowerSoil™ DNA isolation kit (Qiagen). Incubate at 65 °C for 5 min. Vortex 30 s, sonicate 30 s, then vortex with a FastPrep‑24 Classic (MP Biomedicals) for four cycles of 60 s each. Centrifuge the tubes at 13 000 × g for 1 min at room temperature. Transfer the supernatant to a new sterile 2 mL tube and isolate genomic DNA using the DNeasy PowerSoil™ kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Elute DNA in 100 µL RNase/DNase‑free water and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Assess DNA quality and quantity
steps.instruction: Run 1.5 % agarose gel electrophoresis to check DNA integrity. Measure DNA concentration with a NanoDrop 2000 spectrophotometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Record A260/A280 ratios (average ≈ 1.9). Expected concentrations: 45–50 ng µL⁻¹ for water‑filter extracts and 95–100 ng µL⁻¹ for biofilm extracts.

steps.title: Quantify 16S rDNA by ddPCR
steps.instruction: Set up 25 µL ddPCR reactions using QX200™ EvaGreen Supermix (Bio‑Rad) on a Bio‑Rad CFX96™ Real‑Time system. Each reaction contains 12.5 µL EvaGreen Supermix, 2.5 µL nuclease‑free water, 2.5 µL (10 µM) of each primer (519f/Ba907r), 2.5 µL BSA, and 5.0 µL of DNA diluted ten‑fold. Run the thermal program: 95 °C for 15 min, then 40 cycles of 95 °C for 60 s, 52 °C for 60 s, and 72 °C for 60 s. Analyse droplets to obtain bacterial 16S copy numbers.

steps.title: Culture and enumerate E. coli
steps.instruction: Inoculate Escherichia coli reference strains into Luria‑Bertani (LB) broth and incubate at 37 °C with shaking at 100 rpm. Monitor growth by measuring optical density at 600 nm (OD600). For viable counts, perform serial dilutions in LB broth, spread 50 µL of each dilution onto LB agar plates in duplicate, and incubate plates at 37 °C for 24 h. Count colonies only on plates with 20–300 colonies and calculate CFU mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Extract DNA from E. coli cultures
steps.instruction: Harvest E. coli cells and extract genomic DNA using the DNeasy Blood & Tissue kit (Qiagen) according to the supplier’s protocol. Perform lysis by adding 100 µL lysozyme (500 µg mL⁻¹) and incubating 5 min at room temperature before proceeding with the kit steps.

steps.title: Prepare qPCR reactions for target genes
steps.instruction: For each target (total bacteria, archaea, AOA, AOB, Nitrospira, Nitrobacter) prepare duplicate reactions using either GoTaq (Promega) or FastStart (Roche) polymerase as specified in Table 1. Include a standard curve ranging from 5 to 5 × 10⁹ copies per reaction.

substeps.instruction: GoTaq mix (25 µL total): 2 µL DNA template, 0.2 µM each primer, 0.2 µM dNTPs, 2.5 mM MgCl₂, 3.34 µM SYTO® 9, 1× GoTaq buffer, 1 U GoTaq DNA polymerase, add nuclease‑free water to 25 µL.
FastStart mix (20 µL total): 2 µL DNA template, 0.5 µM each primer, 3.34 µM SYTO® 9, 1× FastStart Essential Probe Master, add nuclease‑free water to 20 µL.
Initial denaturation: GoTaq – 95 °C for 3 min; FastStart – 95 °C for 10 min.

Cycling conditions (example for bacteria with GoTaq): 40 cycles of 95 °C for 20 s, 60 °C for 20 s, 72 °C for 30 s. Use the specific annealing temperatures and cycle numbers listed for each primer set in Table 1.

steps.title: Run qPCR and analyse data
steps.instruction: Load reactions onto a LightCycler® 96 instrument and run the programmed thermal profile. Use the LightCycler® 96 software to generate standard curves, calculate amplification efficiency (Eff = 10^(–1/slope) – 1), determine R² (≥ 0.99), and obtain copy numbers per µL. Verify melt curves to confirm product specificity and check that non‑template controls have Ct ≈ 40 while internal positive controls (E. coli ATCC 25922) have Ct ≈ 25.
